thread:
Maria Chen: quick sync - we're finalizing SDK error handling. Goals: surface request ids, keep raw payload accessible, and differentiate stream vs API errors. want language-specific guidance + retry rules.

Jon Rivera: +1 to surfacing request id and raw payload. Minimal JS error shape: `name`, `message`, `requestId`, `raw`. keep `raw` as the entire server JSON for debugging but only include at debug log level. Example: 
```js
class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(code, msg, requestId, raw) {
    super(msg); this.name = code; this.requestId = requestId; this.raw = raw;
  }
}
```

Alex Kim: Go should return typed errors, not panics. Something like: 
```go
type APIError struct {
  Code string
  Message string
  RequestID string
  Raw string // JSON dump
}
func (e *APIError) Error() string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s", e.Code, e.Message) }
```
keep it small so callers can switch on Code.

Priya Singh: streaming edgecases: if a stream ends mid-response (EOF) emit StreamTruncated or StreamInterrupted. mark as retryable only if server provides a resumable token or client kept state (cursor/kv). otherwise treat as non-auto-retry and surface partial output. users should opt-in to auto-resume.

Maria Chen: header strategy? set `Redwood-Request-Id` vs `X-Request-Id`? and on retries, reuse or mint a new id?

Jon Rivera: send both headers with the same v4 UUID for the initial attempt for compatibility. on retry, mint a new request id but include `original_request_id` in the metadata/payload so server logs can correlate attempts. that keeps each attempt distinct while preserving linkage.

Alex Kim: logging: always include requestId and spanId where available. logs should look like: `logger.error("api error", { code, route, requestId, spanId })`. raw server body only at trace/debug. also capture the request headers for debugging auth issues.

Priya Singh: retry policy summary: auto-retry only for network failures and 5xx on idempotent endpoints. do NOT auto-retry 4xx except maybe 429 with Retry-After handled. for streaming reconnects, only auto-resume if SDK has explicit resume token and user enabled resume. otherwise bubble up.

Maria Chen: mapping server codes to SDK classes: we could expose a small set of typed errors (AuthError, RateLimitError, StreamError) and otherwise provide ApiError with a `code` field. pros: easy `catch (e instanceof RateLimitError)`; cons: too many classes if we mirror every server type. lean small.

SRE-Bot: reminder: server indexing depends on request_id/span_id. please generate proper v4 uuids in SDKs and avoid user-supplied short ids.

Jon Rivera: also, if server returns request_id in the error payload attach that to the exception. fallback: capture the id the SDK sent.

Priya Singh: testing matrix idea Maria: 1) produce 400/401/403/429 shapes -> ensure correct typed error mapping; 2) 500 and network failures -> ensure retry/no-retry behavior; 3) streaming EOF vs server stream-error -> surface different types; 4) header propagation and original_request_id on retries.

Maria Chen: great. I'll write a short RFC (node/py/go snippets + tests) and include specific header names and fields. planning to include an optional `resume` API for streams that returns a token.

ci-bot: created branch `devex/sdker-rid-retries-stream-resume` and opened PR #412 - https://git.company/repo/pulls/412

Jon Rivera: I'll review the PR tomorrow, leaving comments on the python sketch.

Alex Kim: one last note: in Go, include helper functions to inspect errors without type assertions: `IsRateLimit(err)`/`GetRequestID(err)` so callers in non-exception languages can still get structured info.

Maria Chen: perfect — thanks all :thumbsup:
